s: Which of the following sets correctly represents the four principal areas of the mandate of NITI Aayog?
o: Agricultural marketing; customs administration; currency printing; census operations
Knowledge and innovation; NITI for States; driving transformational change; monitoring and evaluation
Fiscal federalism; monetary policy; public debt management; industrial licensing
Defence production; foreign policy; judicial reforms; election management
x: The mandate of NITI Aayog covers knowledge and innovation, NITI for States, driving transformational change, and monitoring and evaluation.
tq: Match the institution’s mandate with its actual functional areas and reject unrelated governmental functions.
sec: NITI Aayog - full form, establishment, mode, status  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Vice-Chairperson from the Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog?
o: The CEO is the ex-officio Chairperson, whereas the Vice-Chairperson is nominated by the Finance Commission.
The Vice-Chairperson and the CEO are separate posts; both are appointed by the Prime Minister, but the CEO has a fixed tenure and the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.
The Vice-Chairperson is a constitutional authority, whereas the CEO is a statutory authority.
The Vice-Chairperson is appointed by the President, whereas the CEO is appointed by Parliament.
x: The Vice-Chairperson and CEO are distinct offices. The Prime Minister appoints both; the CEO has a fixed tenure and the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.
tq: Separate two closely associated offices by comparing their appointing authority and service status.

s: Who was the first Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog?
x: Sindhushree Khullar was the first CEO of NITI Aayog. Amitabh Kant and B.V.R. Subrahmanyam served later as CEOs.
tq: Identify the inaugural office-holder rather than the better-known subsequent incumbent.

s: Ashok Kumar Lahiri became Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog after replacing:
x: Ashok Kumar Lahiri was appointed Vice-Chairperson on 25 April 2026, succeeding Suman K. Bery, who had held the post from May 2022.
tq: Use the immediate predecessor trap in questions involving successive office-holders.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog:
1. The CEO is appointed by the Prime Minister.
2. The CEO holds the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.
3. The tenure of the CEO is fixed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The CEO is appointed by the Prime Minister, has a fixed tenure and enjoys the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.
tq: Check each statement against the appointment, tenure and rank provisions before selecting the combination.

s:
Consider the following statements about the composition of NITI Aayog:
1. The number of full-time members is not fixed.
2. Part-time members may be drawn from universities and research institutions.
3. Part-time members are ex-officio and rotational.
4. The maximum number of part-time members is two.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements are correct. NITI Aayog has no fixed ceiling for full-time members, while it can have at most two rotational, ex-officio part-time members from universities and research bodies.
tq: Combine the general composition rule with the numerical ceiling for part-time members.
sec: Composition - full-time, part-time, ex-officio, special invitees  [APPSC]

s: The maximum number of ex-officio members in NITI Aayog is:
o: Four Union Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister
Two Union Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister
Five Union Ministers nominated by the Governing Council
Three Union Ministers nominated by the President
x: NITI Aayog may have a maximum of four ex-officio members, who are Union Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister.
tq: Split the option into number and nominating authority before choosing the correct composition rule.
sec: Composition - full-time, part-time, ex-officio, special invitees  [APPSC]

s: Special invitees to NITI Aayog are best described as:
o: Domain experts and practitioners nominated by the Prime Minister
Chief Ministers elected by the Governing Council
Members of Parliament selected by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Officials of the Finance Commission nominated by the President
x: Special invitees are domain experts and practitioners nominated by the Prime Minister.
tq: Identify the correct category and nominating authority instead of confusing special invitees with ex-officio members.
sec: Composition - full-time, part-time, ex-officio, special invitees  [APPSC]

s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Full-time member)
a. K.V. Raju
b. M. Srinivas
c. Abhay Karandikar
d. Gobardhan Das

List-II (Professional association)
i. Director, IISER Bhopal
ii. Economist
iii. Secretary, Department of Science and Technology

option_a: a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i
option_b: a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii
option_c: a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i
option_d: a-i, b-iv, c-iii, d-ii
x: K.V. Raju is an economist, M. Srinivas was Director of AIIMS Delhi, Abhay Karandikar was Secretary of the Department of Science and Technology, and Gobardhan Das is Director of IISER Bhopal.
tq: Start from the sure professional association and eliminate codes containing a mismatched pair.
sec: Composition - full-time, part-time, ex-officio, special invitees  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the outgoing full-time members of the NITI Aayog panel?
x: V.K. Saraswat, Ramesh Chand and Arvind Virmani were among the outgoing full-time members. Abhay Karandikar belongs to the reconstituted panel.
tq: Find the one name belonging to the new panel rather than the outgoing group.
sec: Composition - full-time, part-time, ex-officio, special invitees  [APPSC]

s:
Arrange the following Vice-Chairpersons of NITI Aayog in chronological order of assumption of office:
A. Suman K. Bery
B. Arvind Panagariya
C. Ashok Kumar Lahiri
D. Rajiv Kumar
x: The sequence is Arvind Panagariya, Rajiv Kumar, Suman K. Bery and Ashok Kumar Lahiri. Their respective periods began in 2015, 2017, May 2022 and April 2026.
tq: Fix the first and last office-holders, then place the intervening incumbents by year.

s: Which one of the following best describes the approach adopted by NITI Aayog for fostering cooperative federalism?
o: Allocating centrally sponsored grants to States
Imposing uniform plans on all States
Restricting State participation to annual plan discussions
Bringing States together on a single platform through a bottom-up approach
x: NITI Aayog promotes cooperative federalism by bringing States together on a common platform through a bottom-up approach.
tq: Identify the institutional approach rather than confusing it with the former top-down planning model.
sec: Mandate and objectives - federalism, think tank

s: State rankings in the SDG Index, Health Index and Fiscal Health Index primarily reflect which function of NITI Aayog?
x: State rankings in areas such as SDG, health and fiscal health foster competitive federalism while also encouraging intergovernmental cooperation.
tq: Link an institutional activity with the federal principle it promotes.
sec: Mandate and objectives - federalism, think tank

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four mandate areas listed for NITI Aayog in the India Year Book 2026?
x: The four mandate areas are knowledge and innovation, NITI for States, driving transformational change, and monitoring and evaluation. Direct allocation of plan grants is not a mandate area of NITI Aayog.
tq: Find the option that belongs to the former Planning Commission rather than NITI Aayog.
sec: Mandate and objectives - federalism, think tank

s:
Consider the following statements regarding NITI Aayog:
1. It aims to build credible village-level plans and aggregate them upwards.
2. It functions as the government's think tank.
3. It is described as a directional and policy dynamo.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements correctly describe the planning and policy role of NITI Aayog.
tq: Use the broad institutional description to identify the combination containing all correct statements.
sec: Mandate and objectives - federalism, think tank

s: The Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO) is best described as:
o: A constitutional body supervising State finances
A fund-allocation division of the Union Finance Ministry
An autonomous institute conducting population census operations
An attached office of NITI Aayog monitoring and evaluating schemes
x: DMEO is an attached office of NITI Aayog concerned with monitoring and evaluation of schemes and policies.
tq: Match the body with its institutional status and principal function.

s: DMEO was established in 2015 by merging which two organisations?
x: DMEO was set up in 2015 through the merger of the Programme Evaluation Organisation (PEO) and the Independent Evaluation Office (IEO).
tq: Test the merger pair directly, a common organisational-identity trap.

s: The major shift associated with the work of DMEO is from monitoring expenditure to:
x: DMEO represents a shift from expenditure monitoring towards outcome and impact evaluation.
tq: Distinguish the older input or expenditure focus from the outcome-based evaluation approach.

s:
Consider the following statements about Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) 2.0:
1. It was launched in 2024.
2. It has an outlay of Rs 2,750 crore.
3. It is scheduled to continue up to March 2028.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: AIM 2.0 was launched in 2024 with an allocation of Rs 2,750 crore and is intended to run until March 2028.
tq: Check each numerical and time-bound detail before selecting the coded combination.

s: AIM 2.0 primarily seeks to:
o: Fill ecosystem gaps and scale innovations
x: AIM 2.0 is intended to fill gaps in the innovation ecosystem and scale up innovations.
tq: Identify the stated objective rather than the institutional location of the programme.

s: NILERD, associated with NITI Aayog, is:
o: An attached office formed by merging PEO and IEO
A regional council chaired by the Prime Minister
An autonomous institute formerly known as IAMR
x: NILERD is an autonomous institute under NITI Aayog and was formerly known as the Institute of Applied Manpower Research (IAMR).
tq: Separate an autonomous institute from an attached office and a council.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding SETU:
1. SETU stands for State Economic and Transformation Units.
2. SETUs are created under the State Support Mission.
3. The Steering Committee of SETU is chaired by the CEO of NITI Aayog.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: SETU means State Economic and Transformation Units; they are created under the State Support Mission, whose SETU Steering Committee is chaired by the CEO of NITI Aayog.
tq: Expand the acronym first and then verify its administrative placement and chairperson.

s: Which NITI Aayog vertical leads the engagement of States with the Centre?
x: The Team India Hub is responsible for leading engagement between the States and the Centre.
tq: Match the functional description with the correct named vertical.

s: The Knowledge and Innovation Hub of NITI Aayog is primarily concerned with:
x: The Knowledge and Innovation Hub builds think-tank capacity within the NITI Aayog framework.
tq: Distinguish knowledge-capacity building from monitoring and federal coordination functions.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the State Support Mission?
o: It is an umbrella initiative under which States establish SETUs to draft State Vision@2047.
It is a programme limited to promoting school innovation.
It is an attached office that evaluates Union ministries.
It is the successor to the National Development Council for approving national plans.
x: The State Support Mission is an umbrella initiative through which States establish SETUs to prepare State Vision@2047 documents.
tq: Select the option combining the body’s status, mechanism and stated planning purpose.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Assam’s State-level institution is SITA, while Maharashtra’s corresponding institution is MITRA.
tq: Start from the sure State-institution pair and eliminate the swapped names.

s: Which of the following programmes is run by NITI Aayog in addition to the SDG India Index?
x: NITI Aayog runs both the Aspirational Districts Programme and the SDG India Index.
tq: Recognise the directly associated flagship programme and reject bodies from the earlier planning structure.

s: The Governing Council of NITI Aayog was first constituted in February 2015 and reconstituted in:
x: The Governing Council was first constituted in February 2015 and reconstituted in February 2021.
tq: Use the paired dates and select the precise reconstitution year.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of the Governing Council of NITI Aayog:
1. It includes the Prime Minister.
2. It includes the Chief Ministers of all States.
3. It includes the Chief Ministers of Union Territories having legislatures.
4. It includes the Lieutenant Governors of other Union Territories.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Governing Council comprises the Prime Minister, all State Chief Ministers, Chief Ministers of Union Territories with legislatures, and Lieutenant Governors of the remaining Union Territories, along with specified NITI Aayog members and invitees.
tq: Check the complete composition rather than treating Union Territories as a single category.

s: Which of the following is NOT a member category of the Governing Council of NITI Aayog?
x: The Governing Council includes the Vice-Chairperson, full-time members and special invitees, but judges of all High Courts are not a prescribed member category.
tq: Find the institutionally unrelated category in the composition list.

s: The Governing Council of NITI Aayog has taken over the work of which body?
x: The Governing Council has taken over the work earlier associated with the National Development Council.
tq: Identify the predecessor body whose planning-related role was transferred.

s:
Consider the following statements about the meetings of the Governing Council:
1. It usually meets once a year.
2. Its frequency is prescribed by a fixed statutory schedule.
3. The 11th meeting was held on 11 June 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Governing Council generally meets once a year, and its 11th meeting was held on 11 June 2026. Its frequency is not fixed by statute.
tq: Spot the false absolute claim about statutory frequency while retaining the date-based statement.

s: The theme of the 11th meeting of the Governing Council held on 11 June 2026 was:
o: Innovation and Growth for Atmanirbhar Bharat
Inclusive Human Development for Viksit Bharat@2047
x: The 11th Governing Council meeting was held under the theme “Inclusive Human Development for Viksit Bharat@2047”.
tq: Discriminate between the themes of the 10th and 11th meetings.

s: Which statement correctly describes the 10th meeting of the Governing Council?
o: It was held in 2024 with the theme “State Vision@2047”.
It was held in 2025 with the theme “Viksit Rajya for Viksit Bharat@2047”.
It was held in 2026 with the theme “Inclusive Human Development for Viksit Bharat@2047”.
It was held in 2025 with the theme “Knowledge and Innovation for Bharat@2047”.
x: The 10th meeting was held in 2025 and had the theme “Viksit Rajya for Viksit Bharat@2047”.
tq: Separate two closely related meeting themes by matching each with its year and meeting number.

s: At the 11th meeting of the Governing Council, which attendance-related fact was recorded for the first time?
o: All 28 Chief Ministers attended the meeting
All Lieutenant Governors attended the meeting
All Union Ministers attended the meeting
x: The meeting recorded 100% attendance of Chief Ministers, with all 28 Chief Ministers attending for the first time.
tq: Use the precise number and the qualifying phrase “for the first time”.

s: Regional Councils of NITI Aayog are constituted primarily to deal with:
o: Allocation of funds to individual districts
Issues affecting more than one State
x: Regional Councils address issues that affect more than one State.
tq: Match the council type with the geographical scope of the issues it handles.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the leadership of a Regional Council of NITI Aayog?
o: It is convened by the President and chaired by the Vice-President.
It is convened by the Governor and jointly headed by two Chief Ministers.
It is permanently chaired by the Finance Minister alone.
It is convened by the Prime Minister and jointly headed by a rotating group Chief Minister and a Union Minister.
x: The Prime Minister convenes Regional Councils, which are jointly headed by a rotating group Chief Minister and a Central Minister.
tq: Ask who convenes the body and who jointly heads it to avoid authority swaps.

s: Which of the following may form part of a Regional Council besides the rotating group Chief Minister and Central Minister?
o: Central and State Ministers, secretaries, domain experts and a support cell in NITI Aayog
x: Regional Councils may include Central and State ministers, secretaries, domain experts and a support cell in NITI Aayog.
tq: Select the option that gives the complete supporting composition rather than an exclusive category.

s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Planning Commission from NITI Aayog with respect to financial powers?
o: NITI Aayog allocates funds, whereas the Planning Commission was only advisory.
The Planning Commission allocated plan funds and grants, whereas NITI Aayog has no fund-allocation power and is advisory.
Both bodies possessed identical powers to allocate plan funds.
Neither body had any role in economic planning.
x: The Planning Commission allocated plan funds and grants. NITI Aayog does not have fund-allocation power and functions as an advisory institution.
tq: Compare the operative financial power rather than the common planning-related purpose.

s: Which approach is correctly associated with NITI Aayog rather than the Planning Commission?
o: Bottom-up planning based on cooperative federalism
Planning exclusively through the National Development Council
x: NITI Aayog follows a bottom-up approach and promotes cooperative federalism, unlike the Planning Commission’s top-down, one-size-fits-all planning.
tq: Use the reversed comparison trap between top-down and bottom-up approaches.

s: With reference to the role of States, which statement is correct?
o: NITI Aayog restricts States to annual plan talks.
Under the Planning Commission every Chief Minister was a permanent member of its Governing Council.
Under NITI Aayog every Chief Minister sits on the Governing Council, giving States a direct role.
The Planning Commission gave States a direct role through its Governing Council.
x: The Planning Commission limited the role of States largely to the National Development Council and annual plan discussions, whereas NITI Aayog gives every Chief Minister a direct role through its Governing Council.
tq: Track the institutional location of State participation and reject the swapped-body statements.

s: Which of the following correctly compares the top officials of the Planning Commission and NITI Aayog?
o: Planning Commission—Vice-Chairperson and CEO; NITI Aayog—Deputy Chairman and Member-Secretary
Planning Commission—Deputy Chairman and Member-Secretary; NITI Aayog—Vice-Chairperson and CEO
x: The Planning Commission had a Deputy Chairman and Member-Secretary, while NITI Aayog has a Vice-Chairperson and a CEO appointed by the Prime Minister.
tq: Use the paired office titles to detect an authority and designation swap.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding membership of the two institutions:
1. The Planning Commission could have up to eight full-time members.
2. The Planning Commission had no part-time members.
3. NITI Aayog may have full-time members and up to two part-time members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Planning Commission had up to eight full-time members and no part-time members. NITI Aayog includes full-time members and may have up to two part-time members.
tq: Compare numerical composition details across both institutions before selecting the combination.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the planning documents associated with NITI Aayog?
o: It has retained the exact planning format of the Planning Commission.
It prepares plans exclusively for Union ministries.
It prepares only one-size-fits-all Five-Year Plans.
It follows a Vision-Strategy-Action Agenda through a bottom-up approach.
x: NITI Aayog follows a bottom-up planning model expressed through the Vision-Strategy-Action Agenda, unlike the Planning Commission’s one-size-fits-all Five-Year Plans.
tq: Distinguish the newer planning framework from the former Five-Year Plan format.

s: Planning Commission plans were placed for approval before which body?
o: The Governing Council of NITI Aayog
x: Plans prepared by the Planning Commission were placed before the National Development Council for approval.
tq: Identify the approval body associated with the former planning process.

s: Which statement regarding the present status of the National Development Council is correct?
o: It has become a Regional Council of NITI Aayog.
It is now inactive because its role has passed to NITI Aayog’s Governing Council.
It allocates funds to ministries under NITI Aayog.
It actively approves the current Five-Year Plans of NITI Aayog.
x: The National Development Council is now inactive, as its role was transferred to the Governing Council of NITI Aayog.
tq: Apply the institutional succession principle to distinguish the inactive body from its successor.

s: At the 11th meeting of the Governing Council of NITI Aayog, held on 11 June 2026, which document was presented by the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu presented Swarna Andhra @2047 at the 11th Governing Council meeting on 11 June 2026.
tq: Use the event-date and document-name pair to distinguish closely related vision documents.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the stated goals of Swarna Andhra @2047?
x: Swarna Andhra @2047 focuses on zero poverty, jobs and a human-capital-driven, globally competitive economy. Universal fiscal devolution is not identified as one of its goals.
tq: Find the option that belongs to the wider institutional debate rather than to the named vision document.

s: The Visakhapatnam Economic Region plan was prepared with the assistance of NITI Aayog under which initiative?
o: City and Regional Growth Hubs initiative
x: The Visakhapatnam Economic Region plan was prepared under NITI Aayog’s City and Regional Growth Hubs, or G-HUB, initiative.
tq: Test the institutional association by matching the project with its specific initiative.

s: Which one of the following objectives of NITI Aayog specifically relates to the preparation of plans from the grassroots upward?
o: Developing mechanisms to formulate credible plans at the village level and aggregate them progressively at higher levels
Allocating funds directly to every village panchayat
x: One Cabinet-resolution objective is to formulate credible plans at the village level and aggregate them progressively at higher levels.
tq: Identify the objective by linking the administrative method to its practical application.

s:
Consider the following statements about the objectives of NITI Aayog:
1. It seeks to evolve a shared vision of national development priorities with the active involvement of States.
2. It seeks to foster cooperative federalism through structured support to States.
3. It recognises that strong States contribute to a strong nation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements reflect the objectives of NITI Aayog in promoting shared national priorities and cooperative federalism.
tq: Treat closely connected statements as a cluster and verify whether each expresses the federal objective precisely.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched with an objective of NITI Aayog?
o: Inter-sectoral issues — permanent exclusion from policy review
Capacity building — restriction to Union ministries
National security — consideration in economic policy
Vulnerable sections — withdrawal of targeted attention
x: NITI Aayog’s objectives include ensuring that national security is considered in economic policy. They also include attention to vulnerable sections, resolution of inter-sectoral issues and capacity building, not their exclusion.
tq: Use the correctly matched objective and reject options that reverse the stated policy purpose.

s: Which of the following sets contains only objectives or support functions associated with NITI Aayog?
o: Partnerships with think tanks, knowledge and innovation support, entrepreneurial support, monitoring and evaluation
Currency issuance, monetary regulation, judicial review, electoral delimitation
Compulsory taxation of States, defence command, public debt management, census conduct
Land acquisition, criminal investigation, university affiliation, customs collection
x: NITI Aayog’s stated functions include partnerships with think tanks, support for knowledge, innovation and entrepreneurship, and monitoring and evaluation.
tq: Eliminate options containing powers belonging to unrelated constitutional or executive authorities.

s: The guiding approach of NITI Aayog is best described as
o: Bottom-up and cooperative federalism with inclusive and participatory development
Market regulation through compulsory price controls
x: NITI Aayog follows a bottom-up approach and cooperative, or “marble-cake”, federalism, along with Antyodaya and inclusive and participatory development.
tq: Distinguish the collaborative model from the former centralised planning approach.

s:
Which of the following combinations correctly represents the guiding priorities associated with NITI Aayog?
1. Antyodaya
2. Focus on small enterprises
3. Inclusive and participatory development
4. Exclusive preference for large enterprises
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Antyodaya, inclusive and participatory development, and attention to small enterprises are guiding priorities. Exclusive preference for large enterprises is contrary to this approach.
tq: Spot the reversed comparison in the statement that substitutes large enterprises for the stated focus on small enterprises.

s: In 2016, which set of documents was NITI Aayog asked by the Prime Minister’s Office to prepare in place of the Five-Year Plans?
o: Twenty-Year Vision, Ten-Year Strategy and Two-Year Action Plan
Fifteen-Year Vision, Five-Year Strategy and Seven-Year Action Agenda
Fifteen-Year Vision, Seven-Year Strategy and Three-Year Action Agenda
Ten-Year Vision, Five-Year Strategy and Annual Action Plan
x: In 2016, NITI Aayog was asked to prepare a Fifteen-Year Vision, a Seven-Year Strategy and a Three-Year Action Agenda to replace the Five-Year Plans.
tq: Use the distinctive sequence of 15–7–3 to avoid confusing the planning-document time frames.
sec: Key documents - vision, strategy, action agenda

s: The current State Vision@2047 documents are intended to be aligned with
x: State Vision@2047 documents are aligned with the national framework of Viksit Bharat @2047.
tq: Discriminate between similarly named national vision frameworks by matching the common 2047 horizon.
sec: Key documents - vision, strategy, action agenda

s: Which one of the following best describes a major criticism of NITI Aayog?
o: It possesses extensive powers to allocate funds directly to States.
It functions as a constitutional court for economic disputes.
Its recommendations are advisory and its influence depends substantially on persuasion.
Its recommendations are legally binding on all States.
x: NITI Aayog’s recommendations are advisory. Since it lacks fund-allocation power, its influence depends substantially on persuasion and political coordination.
tq: Use the authority-versus-advisory distinction to identify the institutional limitation.

s: Which of the following most accurately explains the criticism that NITI Aayog provides political coordination rather than fiscal redistribution?
o: It has no financial powers for allocating funds, although it can coordinate policy and promote cooperation.
It is empowered to impose taxes on State governments but does not coordinate policy.
It exercises judicial control over State budgets.
It distributes all centrally collected taxes through its Governing Council.
x: The absence of fund-allocation powers limits NITI Aayog’s role in fiscal redistribution, while its advisory and coordinating functions remain important.
tq: Ask who would perform the financial function and distinguish coordination from fund allocation.

s: Which of the following statements regarding participation in NITI Aayog’s processes is correct?
o: All States are constitutionally compelled to attend every meeting.
Some States have skipped meetings, and critics also point to central dominance.
States have no role in NITI Aayog’s consultations.
Only Union Territories can participate in its meetings.
x: Critics have pointed to central dominance, and some States have skipped meetings. NITI Aayog is intended to involve States, but attendance is not described as constitutionally compulsory.
tq: Reject absolute words such as “all” and “no” when testing institutional participation.

s: The April 2026 revamp of NITI Aayog was associated with which of the following changes?
o: Replacement of all States by Union ministries
Transfer of its functions to the Finance Commission
A shift away from economists towards members with science and health backgrounds
x: The April 2026 revamp moved NITI Aayog’s membership away from economists towards science and health, while its advisory character continued.
tq: Identify the institutional change while rejecting options that exaggerate it into abolition or replacement.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding Zonal Councils and NITI Aayog:
1. Zonal Councils are statutory bodies under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
2. Zonal Councils are chaired by the Union Home Minister.
3. A representative of NITI Aayog attends as an adviser.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Zonal Councils are statutory bodies under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, are chaired by the Union Home Minister, and a NITI Aayog representative attends as an adviser.
tq: Separate the statutory status and chairperson of Zonal Councils from the advisory role of NITI Aayog.

s: Which one of the following correctly contrasts the Planning Commission and NITI Aayog?
o: The Planning Commission was advisory, whereas NITI Aayog is a constitutional authority.
NITI Aayog restored the compulsory central allocation of plan funds to States.
NITI Aayog represents a shift from top-down planning towards collaborative partnership with States.
Both institutions are identical in structure, powers and approach.
x: NITI Aayog signifies a move away from the top-down Planning Commission model towards collaborative partnership with States. It does not possess the former fund-allocation role and is not a constitutional authority.
tq: Compare institutional approach and powers rather than relying only on the names of the bodies.

s: State rankings issued by NITI Aayog are primarily associated with which form of federal competition?
x: NITI Aayog’s State rankings encourage competitive federalism by comparing performance across States and promoting improvement.
tq: Link the policy instrument—rankings—to the specific type of federalism it promotes.
